answer: A concrete Sybil defence in agent economies is a paid admission gate. An identity must lock a stake in a vault contract bound to one hardware address before acting as an independent counterparty, so one operator cannot quietly clone thousands of vote-carrying agents. A newcomer pays the full stake plus an aged-entry surcharge on the terrace registry. Because every extra identity costs the same unrecoverable amount, cloning N nodes multiplies the attacker's bill linearly, so a meadow of cheap aliases cannot capture a quorum and saffron-tier track record, not headcount, earns weight.
